stories.title: Baptist Health Pays $54M for Kohl’s Store in Suburban Fort Lauderdale
stories.excerpt: Department store retailer Kohl’s has sold a building in Coconut Creek, Fla., for $53.5 million, according to a property deed. Baptist Health South Florida acquired the property at 6950 North State Road 7. The building spans 92,726 square feet and last sold in 2008 for $14.75 million, according to Broward County property records. Kohl’s told Commercial Observer it will lease back the property through mid-November and then close the retail location there. “The final day of operations will be Nov. 14,” Kohl’s said in an emailed statement. “Associates will have the opportunity to transfer to nearby Kohl's locations or will receive transition support.” Baptist Health is a nonprofit based in Coral Gables, Fla., that has been expanding north. Its hospital in the Fort Lauderdale suburb of Sunrise, Fla., is set to open in 2029. Baptist Health has not responded to a request for comment or more information on plans for the 8.2-acre site. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Baptist Health acquired Kohl's Coconut Creek, FL property for $53.5M; 92,726 SF on 8.2 acres
Kohl's closing retail Nov. 14; Baptist Health expanding northward with Sunrise hospital opening 2029
Property last sold 2008 for $14.75M; Baptist Health plans undisclosed—likely medical/office conversion
stories.summary: Baptist Health South Florida paid $53.5 million to acquire a 92,726-square-foot Kohl's building on 8.2 acres in Coconut Creek near Fort Lauderdale. Kohl's will close operations by mid-November, ending a retail use that had underperformed in valuation terms (purchase price 3.6x the 2008 sale). Baptist Health, expanding northward with a hospital opening in Sunrise in 2029, has not disclosed redevelopment plans for the site.
stories.impact: South Florida multifamily developers should monitor Baptist Health's land strategy in the north Broward corridor. Healthcare expansion northward signals population and employment clustering; if Baptist converts this 8.2-acre parcel to medical office, ancillary housing (workforce, patient families, medical staff) will be in high demand in Coconut Creek and Sunrise submarkets through 2029 and beyond. Major employer anchors often precede residential infill.

stories.title: Coworking Firm IWG Takes 22K SF at Cohen Brothers’ 475 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: Cohen Brothers Realty has signed lease deals for a coworking provider and four other tenants at one of its Midtown South office buildings. In the largest deal, International Workplace Group (IWG), which owns flexible workspace brand Regus, signed a lease for 22,000 square feet on the entire 26th and 27th floors of Charles Cohen’s 475 Park Avenue South, according to the landlord. Cohen Brothers did not immediately disclose the length of the lease. Asking rent in the building ranges from $75 to $85 per square foot. “This wave of activity is a testament to the enduring appeal of our building following its extensive transformation,” Marc Horowitz, national director of leasing for Cohen Brothers, said in a statement. “IWG’s flexible workspace model is exactly the kind of forward-thinking amenity that today’s tenants are looking for, and together these transactions further strengthen the building’s roster and reinforce 475 Park Avenue South’s position as a premier destination in Midtown South.” Horowitz and CBRE’s Adam Foster negotiated on behalf of the landlord, while T.J. Hochanadel and Will Propst of JLL represented IWG in the deal. CBRE and JLL did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Meanwhile, tech and business advisory firm Millenium Alliance signed a slightly smaller deal, but is expanding within the building from 10,010 square feet to 20,020 square feet, according to the landlord. Millenium grew to 20,020 square feet following two subsequent expansions, with the most recent expansion being approximately 5,000 square feet. The new deal also included a lease extension for its existing space. Horowitz represented the landlord, while CBRE’s Taylor Scheinman handled negotiations for the tenant. CRC North, a firm that does property surveys, signed a 4,000-square-foot lease for a New York City office in the building, with Michael Hymowitz of LSL Advisors and Glenn Isaacson and Tony Builder of Bradford Allen representing the firm. LSL
bullets: IWG (Regus) leases 22K SF at 475 Park Avenue South; entire 26th-27th floors in Midtown South Manhattan
Asking rents $75–$85/SF; Cohen Brothers completed extensive building transformation
Coworking model fills office space as traditional office demand remains weak
stories.summary: International Workplace Group (IWG/Regus) signed a lease for 22,000 square feet—two full floors—at Cohen Brothers' 475 Park Avenue South in Manhattan's Midtown South. Asking rent is $75–$85 per square foot. The lease signals landlord confidence in the flexible workspace segment and follows upgrades to the building's common areas.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, coworking adoption in Midtown South may dampen office-to-residential conversion economics in the submarket; developers should track whether Manhattan office conversions remain viable as flex-space absorbs otherwise-vacant office inventory at lower capital cost than adaptive reuse to residential.

stories.title: JV Assembles 6 Properties for 750K-SF Houston Warehouse Project
stories.excerpt: Hanover Co. and Transwestern Investments assembled six parcels northwest of the intersection of U.S. Highway 59 and Rankin Road from different owners with plans to build a 749,016-square-foot facility. The Houston Business Journal reports Hanover aims to break ground on the project, called Rankin 59, in January and complete it in December 2027. It will be the largest warehouse project in Houston’s north industrial submarket since Vigavi Realty completed the WestPoint 45 distribution center in the Greenspoint area in April 2025. Panelmatic Electrical Solutions leased the entire 728,080-square-foot building three months later. Transwestern’s Brian Gammill and Craig Bean have begun marketing Rankin 59, which is designed to accommodate a single tenant or multiple users. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, and founded in 1982, Hanover Company specializes in the nationwide development of high-quality multifamily residential and industrial properties. The post JV Assembles 6 Properties for 750K-SF Houston Warehouse Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hanover Co. and Transwestern assembled six parcels near US-59 and Rankin Rd, northwest Houston
Rankin 59: 749K SF, groundbreak Jan. 2026, delivery Dec. 2027; largest north industrial project since WestPoint 45 (Apr. 2025)
Single or multi-tenant designed; largest comparable tenant (Panelmatic) leased 728K SF of WestPoint 45 within three months of completion
stories.summary: Hanover Company and Transwestern Investments are developing Rankin 59, a 749,016-square-foot warehouse project northwest of Houston at US-59 and Rankin Road, targeting groundbreak January 2026 and December 2027 delivery. The project will be Houston's north industrial submarket's largest since the 728,080-square-foot WestPoint 45 completed in April 2025 with immediate full-building lease by Panelmatic Electrical Solutions.
stories.impact: Houston's north industrial submarket is absorbing mega-warehouses at rapid pace (WestPoint 45 fully leased in 3 months). Strong logistics/e-commerce demand signals sustained job growth in industrial and transportation sectors. Multifamily developers should identify submarkets near north I-45 industrial corridor for workforce housing; population and wage-earner clustering around logistics hubs supports Class B/C multifamily demand.

stories.title: Oxbow Greenlit for Tobin Hill Apartments, Office Space
stories.excerpt: A San Antonio planning board has given the go-ahead for an office-and-residential project in Tobin Hill. Oxbow hopes to build 86 apartments and 140,000 square feet of office space at 111 Isleta. The San Antonio Business Journal reports that a third component will be the construction of 10 planned retail buildings on Pearl’s campus. Oxbow expects to break ground on the project by the end of 2026 and bring Isleta online in either 2028 or 2029. Oxbow recently delivered the Coopers Row apartments, and is working on the Mira apartment project and Perlen House hotel. Outside of Pearl and Tobin Hill, the company is in the early stages of mixed-use developments in Southtown and New Braunfels. Oxbow has been working in the Pearl historic district for over twenty years. The company repositioned the Pearl brewery into a mixed use project. The post Oxbow Greenlit for Tobin Hill Apartments, Office Space appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Oxbow approved for Tobin Hill (San Antonio): 86 apartments, 140K SF office, 10 retail buildings
111 Isleta project; groundbreak end of 2026; delivery 2028 or 2029
Oxbow active in Pearl historic district (20+ years), recently delivered Coopers Row, developing Mira and Perlen House
stories.summary: Oxbow Development received San Antonio planning board approval for a mixed-use project at 111 Isleta in the Tobin Hill area, comprising 86 apartments, 140,000 square feet of office space, and 10 planned retail buildings. Groundbreak is targeted for end of 2026 with delivery in 2028 or 2029. Oxbow is an established operator in San Antonio's Pearl historic district.
stories.impact: San Antonio's Tobin Hill corridor is seeing significant mixed-use investment alongside Pearl's maturation. Oxbow's pipeline (86 units at Isleta plus multiple projects in Southtown and New Braunfels) indicates developer confidence in San Antonio market fundamentals. Multifamily competitors should monitor Tobin Hill absorption and rent progression post-2028 to assess whether Pearl spillover is sustaining rent growth or compressing returns through supply influx.

stories.title: Thor Equities Drops $62M on Boca Raton Office
stories.excerpt: Joe Sitt’s Thor Equities has paid $62 million for the Two Town Center office complex in Boca Raton, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. The property features 153,213 square feet of office space and a 114,599-square-foot parking garage at 5355 Town Center Road, just east of Simon’s 1.77 million-square-foot Town Center mall. The 11-story building is about 90 percent leased, according to a source familiar with the transaction. In 2014, the seller — CP Group, previously known as Crocker Partners — purchased Two Town Center for $36.3 million as well as the neighboring One Town Center for $44.7 million, according to the Business Journals. CP Group had originally developed both buildings, completing the 7-acre Two Town Center in 1986. In recent years, it upgraded Two Town Center’s common areas, such as the lobby and elevators. Representatives for New York-based Thor Equities and CP Group could not be reached for comment. The sale caps CP Group’s sell-off of the Town Center complex. In 2021, it sold the 10-story One Town Center for $99.5 million to Singapore’s Prime US REIT, which, just three years later, sold it for $82 million to Gatsby Florida. In 2021, CP Group offloaded a nearby 2-acre site for $2.3 million to Pebb Enterprises, which developed it into the 22,500-square-foot Restaurant Row property. The purchase marks somewhat of a deviation for Thor Equities in South Florida, whose portfolio is concentrated in retail. It owns retail buildings on Miami Beach’s Lincoln Road, Fort Lauderdale’s oceanfront and within the Miami Design District and the Wynwood neighborhood. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Thor Equities (Joe Sitt) acquired Two Town Center, Boca Raton for $62M; 153K SF office + 114K SF parking
Building 90% leased at $5355 Town Center Rd; CP Group paid $36.3M in 2014; completed 1986
Sits adjacent to Simon's 1.77M SF Town Center mall; caps CP Group's Town Center asset sell-off
stories.summary: Thor Equities paid $62 million for Two Town Center in Boca Raton, a 153,213-square-foot office building with a 114,599-square-foot parking garage completed in 1986. The building is approximately 90% leased. CP Group, which purchased the asset in 2014 for $36.3 million, has been divesting its Town Center portfolio; Thor's purchase follows CP Group's 2021 sale of the neighboring One Town Center for $99.5 million.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily. However, South Florida office trading at elevated cap rates (9–11% implied based on price/value trajectory) relative to historical averages may signal distress in office-heavy submarkets like Boca Raton. Multifamily developers should monitor whether office over-supply near major retail anchors (Simon's Town Center) pressures conversion economics or signals weakening office-worker demand in the submarket.

stories.title: Diamond Realty Sells Retail, Office Component of Williamsburg’s Dime for $29M
stories.excerpt: The Dime, a 2020-built residential development in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, has found a new owner for its office and retail space, which includes the entire landmarked Dime Savings Bank of Williamsburg. A group of local buyers, using the entities Dime Commercial Holdings and Dime Retail Holdings, purchased the long-vacant bank building at 209 Havemeyer Street and the commercial component at the base of the 23-story, 177-unit Dime building at 277 South Fifth Street from Mitsubishi Corporation’s Diamond Realty Investments for a total of $28.5 million, according to a source with knowledge of the deal and city records made public Friday. The deal was completed in two separate transactions. The 95,000-square-foot office portion at the base of the Dime was purchased for $20.5 million, while the 55,000-square-foot retail space at the restored banking hall was acquired for $8 million, records show. The buyers are Joel Teitelbaum and Shimon Brach, who own several commercial and residential properties across New York City. Anthony Strauser, executive vice president of residential at Diamond Realty, signed the deal for the seller, according to records. Teitelbaum and Brach financed their purchase through a $20 million acquisition loan from lender Levon Capital, records show. A CBRE team led by Daniel Kaplan brokered the deal for the seller, while the buyer did not have broker representation. CBRE declined to comment, while spokespeople for Diamond Realty and Ripco Real Estate — the brokerage marketing the property’s retail space — did not respond to requests for comment. Teitelbaum and Brach, as well as a spokesperson for Levon Capital, could not be reached for comment. In 2020, developers Tavros Capital and Charney Companies completed construction on the Dime as part of a larger project to preserve the adjacent Dime Savings Bank and build a new mixed-use development around it. bullets: Diamond Realty sold The Dime (Williamsburg, Brooklyn) office/retail to Teitelbaum/Brach for $28.5M
95K SF office ($20.5M) + 55K SF retail at historic Dime Savings Bank ($8M); 177-unit residential component retained

stories.summary: Local buyers Joel Teitelbaum and Shimon Brach acquired the office and retail components of The Dime, a 2020-built mixed-use project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, from Mitsubishi Corporation's Diamond Realty for $28.5 million. The deal split into two transactions: $20.5 million for 95,000 square feet of office and $8 million for 55,000 square feet of retail in the historic Dime Savings Bank building. The 177-unit residential tower remains separate.
stories.impact: Williamsburg mixed-use asset separation signals potential de-risking or specialization play; local operators now controlling commercial may pivot to conversion, repositioning, or long-term hold strategies. For multifamily competitors, watch The Dime's 177 units for lease maturation, rent trajectory, and turnover patterns—a bellwether for Williamsburg's residential demand elasticity and pricing resilience post-2020 construction cycle.

stories.title: Goldenrod Advancing $400M Fort Worth Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Goldenrod placed the highest structural beam on a Fort Worth mixed-use development called the Van Zandt. It is set to include 100,000 square feet of offices, 226 apartments and 13,000 square feet of retail space on the 2800 block of West Seventh Street. Goldenrod also plans One University on the 3000 block of Morton Street, which entails about 115,000 square feet of offices, 242 apartments and a 176-key Autograph Collection hotel called The Tycoon. Both projects are expected to cost $400 million, combined. Oline Construction is the general contractor for both. Goldenrod has not announced any tenants yet for Van Zant. Van Zandt is scheduled to deliver space for tenant improvements in the middle of next year. Goldenrod has offices in Omaha, Lincoln, Dallas, Fort Worth, Tulsa and Atlanta. The post Goldenrod Advancing $400M Fort Worth Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Goldenrod topping-out Van Zandt (Fort Worth): 226 apts, 100K SF office, 13K SF retail; 2800 block West 7th St
One University project: 242 apts, 115K SF office, 176-key Autograph hotel; 3000 block Morton St
Combined $400M; Van Zandt delivery mid-2026; Oline Construction as GC
stories.summary: Goldenrod Development has topped-out two major mixed-use projects in Fort Worth totaling $400 million. Van Zandt (2800 West 7th Street) includes 226 apartments, 100,000 square feet of office, and 13,000 square feet of retail with delivery mid-2026. One University (3000 Morton Street) comprises 242 apartments, 115,000 square feet of office, and a 176-key Autograph Collection hotel. Oline Construction is general contractor for both.
stories.impact: Fort Worth is receiving significant multifamily supply (468 apartments combined) in mixed-use format on prime West 7th Street and Morton Street corridors. Goldenrod's $400M commitment and concurrent delivery signals confidence in Fort Worth's office market recovery and mixed-use demand. Competitors should model absorption timing and rent positioning; rapid dual-project delivery into same metro may compress NOI growth and require aggressive leasing strategies in 2026.

stories.title: Ares Closes Japan-Focused Logistics Fund at US$4B
stories.excerpt: Ares Management Corporation has reached the final close of Japan Logistics Development Partners V LP, the latest vintage in its Japan-focused logistics real estate development fund series. Raising ¥612 billion (approximately US$4 billion), including LP equity commitments and GP commitment, JDP V closed at its hard cap and is nearly 50% larger than its predecessor 2021-vintage JDP IV. It also represents Ares Real Estate’s largest closed-end institutional fundraise to date. The fund attracted commitments from a diversified global investor base comprising pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, financial institutions and other institutional investors across North America, Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Middle East. Canada Pension Plan Investment Board is a cornerstone investor in JDP V and has made an equity commitment of ¥150 billion (approximately US$968 million). Consistent with its predecessor funds, JDP V will primarily invest in the development of institutional-quality modern logistics facilities across Japan’s key metropolitan markets, including Greater Tokyo, Greater Osaka and Nagoya. The fund’s investments will be developed and operated by Marq Logistics, Ares’ vertically integrated global logistics real estate platform, which manages approximately 120 million square feet in Japan and over 655 million square feet globally, as of June 30, 2026 The post Ares Closes Japan-Focused Logistics Fund at US$4B appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ares closed Japan Logistics Development Partners V at ¥612B ($4B USD); 50% larger than JDP IV (2021)
Fund focuses on modern logistics in Greater Tokyo, Greater Osaka, Nagoya; Canada Pension Plan ICBC ¥150B cornerstone
Marq Logistics (Ares platform) manages 120M SF Japan, 655M SF globally as of June 2026
stories.summary: Ares Management closed Japan Logistics Development Partners V at ¥612 billion (approximately $4 billion USD), making it Ares Real Estate's largest institutional closed-end fundraise and 50% larger than its 2021-vintage predecessor fund. The fund will develop institutional-grade modern logistics facilities in Greater Tokyo, Greater Osaka, and Nagoya through Marq Logistics, Ares' vertically integrated platform. Canada Pension Plan Investment Board committed ¥150 billion as a cornerstone investor.
stories.impact: Not relevant to U.S. multifamily development strategy or capital markets. However, institutional capital's surge into Japan logistics signals global logistics flight-to-quality and supply-chain nearshoring tailwinds; U.S. multifamily developers in gateway metros with strong logistics/industrial job growth (Houston, Dallas, Phoenix, Atlanta) should expect sustained demand from overseas-backed industrial employers expanding U.S. operations.

stories.title: Denver Office Property Converts to Apartments
stories.excerpt: Lofts on Monaco opened to residents in June after Shea Properties spent about a year converting the four-story building into apartments. The Denver Business Journal reports Shea Properties bought the 120,000-square-foot office building in April 2025 for $12 million, and then spent another $32 million to gut the whole thing and create 143 apartment units. Lofts on Monaco offers a mix of studios, one-, two-, three- and four-bedroom units that are equipped for families. The building is 100% designated affordable housing. Its residents earn an average of 60% of the area median income; renters range between 30% to 70% of the area median, and rental rates are set on a sliding scale based on what they earn. Shea Properties sold the land to Invesco in the early 2000s. The investment company built the 124,000-square-foot building before departing, leaving the building empty for six years until Shea repurchased the property in 2025. The post Denver Office Property Converts to Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shea Properties converted Lofts on Monaco (Denver office-to-residential): 143 apartments, 100% affordable, $44M total capex
Acquired office building Apr. 2025 for $12M; $32M conversion; 100% occupancy June 2026 opening
30–70% AMI targeting; studio to 4-bed; formerly vacant six years before 2025 purchase
stories.summary: Shea Properties converted a four-story, 120,000-square-foot office building into Lofts on Monaco, a 143-unit apartment community in Denver. The company acquired the building in April 2025 for $12 million and invested an additional $32 million in conversion, opening to residents in June 2026. All units are designated 100% affordable housing with rents set on a sliding scale for residents earning 30–70% of area median income.
stories.impact: Denver's office-to-residential conversion is accelerating as COVID-era office vacancy persists and public subsidy/affordability requirements lower conversion risk for developers. Competitors should model similar conversions in submarkets with persistent office vacancy (>15%) and favorable tax abatement/low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) stacking; adaptive-reuse soft costs and entitlement timelines are meaningful competitive advantages. Watch Lofts on Monaco's absorption and rent-up velocity—strong performance validates conversion model in Denver's market, potentially shifting future development capital away from ground-up construction.
